rationale: This program is a small (20 functions, ~17.7 KB text) C++ abstraction-penalty benchmark dominated by one enormous main (11.4 KB, ~65% of text) containing tight template-instantiated loops (heapsort, sum, stepanov_abstraction/vector), so the weight table favors low-cost, low-risk passes while restraining the expensive structural ones: SUB and SPLIT get strong benefit weights with minimal cost emphasis because they cheaply diversify arithmetic and basic-block layout across all the template-heavy functions and compose well with other passes; FLA and IBR get solid benefit weights with moderate runtime-cost weight since the benchmark's hot loops can tolerate flattening/dispatch overhead in a test harness but it should still gate application to loop-dominated functions; BCF's benefit weight stays high for the resistance value of opaque predicates in the large main, but its RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are raised because bogus control flow would bloat an already text-heavy binary and slow the measured loops; ICALL is kept with strong diversity weight (indirect calls frustrate static call-graph recovery in this heavily templated, heavily inlined code) tempered by a higher CorrectnessRisk weight given vtable-heavy C++; and IGV is retained at moderate weights since the program's few global benchmark structures offer limited but non-zero value for global-variable transformation with low expected cost.
